results.fact: dist_km (Approach, one way) 22 km vs itinerary day-1 approach 7 mi
results.evidence: Still real on the live row: dist_km 22 km (~13.7 mi) matches the itinerary round trip (13.5 mi in totalNote), not the 7 mi day-1 approach. Published approach descriptions give the leg in pieces (about 3 mi of Stuart Lake Trail to the south branch of Mountaineer Creek, about 2 mi up to the ~5,800 ft head of the valley, then about half a mile to the ridge base; another says 3-4 mi of trail before leaving it), but no source states a single one-way figure, and summing the pieces would be a computed value. dist_km left unchanged.

results.fact: Sherpa south basin camp waypoint elev 6200 vs elevFt 6300
results.evidence: Still present: waypoints[2] stores elev 6200 and elevFt 6300, and bivy[0] of the same name says 6200. The camp is an informal spot with no coordinate on the waypoint, so the ground height cannot be read, and no published elevation for it was found on a second look. The rendered waypoint list uses elev (6200, agreeing with the bivy), so the visible page is already consistent; only the non-rendered elevFt copy differs. No patch without an external figure.

results.correct_value: East Ridge itself Class 3-4 with brief low-5th steps; 5.7 belongs to the optional Balanced Rock
results.evidence: A second look confirms the first pass: the peak's route description gives the East Ridge as Class 3-4 up a broad gully and blocky crest past the balanced rock, with the 5.7 rating attached only to the shoulder-stand/friction climb of the Balanced Rock obelisk; the encyclopedia entry and a 2014 report agree the East Ridge is the least technical line; the route database lists only the North (5.8) and West (5.5) ridges. So rock_grade and overview are right, and grade 'Grade III, 5.7', the 5.5/5.7/5.6 pitch_detail rows (whose crux is placed on a tower below the obelisk, not on the obelisk) and partner_requirements ('sustained 5.7 trad leading') overstate the ridge. Fixing it means rewriting the pitch_detail rows and deciding the commitment numeral (grade says III, commitment says II), for which no source gives a figure; left for a dedicated pass rather than a partial patch.

results.fact: Total elevation gain and loss for the Southwest Route
results.evidence: The live row now says gain_ft 7,000 and loss_ft 5,500, while the itinerary days sum to 8,200 ft gain and 8,400 ft loss and totalNote says 8,000-9,000 ft; the row still disagrees with itself. The only new external figure is a route listing for a different Sinister line (North Face) over the same Downey Creek / Cub Lake approach giving 32 mi and 7,000 ft, which looks like net relief (1,450 ft trailhead to the 8,444 ft summit) rather than a cumulative total; the Northwest Face listing gives 35 mi and 11,400 ft. No two sources agree on the Southwest Route total, and a loss figure may not be set equal to gain by argument alone. No patch.

results.fact: Overview's stated route length (~1,300 ft) is roughly double length_m and the pitch-length total
results.evidence: Still present (overview ~1,300 ft vs length_m 213 m / 4 rows of 35-55 m). A further 2025 report gives six pitches of roughly 60 m each plus a 90 m final traverse, which is longer than both 700 ft and the stored pitch lengths; the first-free-ascent note gives 1,300 ft for the whole line and the route database 700 ft. The sources measure different things and do not converge on one length. No patch.

results.fact: ice grade: ice_grade/alpine_grade WI3 vs grade WI4 and pitch 4 WI4
results.evidence: Still present. Current descriptions give 5.8 WI3 M5- (route database, search-indexed summaries) and a 2025 report grades it III M5 without an ice number; the original ascent was graded WI4. Ice on this line varies strongly from year to year, and no second current source independently gives WI3 or WI4 for the ice step, so the grade field and pitch 4 were not changed.

Pitch counts depend on rope length: 4 long pitches with simul-climbing on a 70 m, 5-6 on a 60 m, and a 2025 party pitched it as six. The header's 5 and the 4-row breakdown both match a published convention, but the page does not say which rope each assumes; no single count is settled by two sources. No patch.

results.fact: Total gain: gain_ft vs itinerary day gains
results.evidence: Still present: gain_ft/loss_ft 6,800 while the itinerary days sum to 7,300 ft gain and 6,400 ft loss. The Northeast Shoulder route listing gives 12 mi and 6,800 ft (matching gain_ft, but from an older, higher start); a 2018 club trip from 1,850 ft gave 4,500 ft to Point 5791 plus 2,800 ft on summit day (~7,300 ft); a trip report from the current low washout parking describes nearly 6,000 ft to Cyclone Lake plus ~2,000 ft to the summit; a GPS log gave ~8,000 ft. The totals depend on where parties parked and no two sources agree on one figure. No patch.

results.correct_value: Glacier route best in late spring / early summer (roughly May-July)
results.evidence: Two sources now point the same way: the Northeast Shoulder route listing calls it a very good early-season climb (May-June) while listing it as available May-October, and the peak's route summary says the Kindy Ridge line uses the Snowking Glacier/snowfield in spring and early summer and the west ridge in late summer and fall. That supports season (May-Jul), gear and pro_tips, and contradicts best_season, seasonal_guidance (August optimal), itinerary.cal (June-September), approach_variants[0].season, seasonal_hazards (avalanche 'N/A' because 'Jul-Sep'; crevasses 'best traveled once well-covered (mid-summer)') and climate. Aligning the row means rewriting the month-by-month guidance, the avalanche block (an early-season window would put the approach inside avalanche season) and several prose fields, which is a rebuild rather than a minimal patch; left for that pass with the direction established.
